themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 10 THIS WEEK, a 1233% spike versus the 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.16), suggesting a sudden public health and sanitation emergency in CD206.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (1233% increase)
Z-score of 11.16 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Concurrent 1500% spike in 'Animal in a Park' complaints last week (4 vs. 0.2 avg)
Concurrent 487% spike in animal-abuse complaints THIS WEEK (11 vs. 1.9 avg)
reporting_angles: Investigation into what triggered the sudden die-off or accumulation of dead animals across the neighborhood
Interview DSNY and Parks Department on response time and disposal protocols
Ground reporting: Are residents observing sick or stressed animal populations, suggesting disease or environmental contamination?

themes_detail.label: Animal Welfare Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Animal-abuse complaints hit 11 THIS WEEK, a 487% spike from the 1.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.17), coinciding with spikes in dead animals and animals in parks, signaling a potential animal welfare crisis.
evidence: 11 animal-abuse complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (487% increase)
Z-score of 5.17 indicates statistically significant spike
Clustered with 10 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK and 4 animals-in-park complaints last week
Pattern suggests systemic animal welfare issue, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Track complaints to specific locations (parks, streets) to identify hotspots
Interview ASPCA and local animal rescue on surge in reported abuse and whether they're seeing it on the ground
Explore whether neglect at shelters or outdoor facilities is contributing

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 16 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1180% spike from the 1.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 12.3), indicating a sustained or emerging vandalism problem in CD206.
evidence: 16 graffiti complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (1180% increase)
Z-score of 12.3 represents highest statistical anomaly in dataset
No current-week data available; recency slightly lower than this-week spikes but severity highest
reporting_angles: Visual survey of Belmont and East Tremont streets to document graffiti clustering and target areas
Interview NYPD and Parks Enforcement on whether gang activity or coordinated tagging campaign is occurring
Follow up: Has DSNY addressed the surge, or are tags still visible two weeks later?

themes_detail.label: Street Light Outages Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 20 LAST WEEK, a 357% spike from the 4.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.91), creating potential safety hazards across the district.
evidence: 20 street light complaints filed last week vs. 4.4 weekly average (357% increase)
Overlaps with spike in 'Obstruction' complaints last week (5 vs. 0.9 avg, 471% increase), suggesting street infrastructure degradation
May correlate with graffiti spike 2 weeks prior (broken lights often tied to areas of disorder)
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify which blocks are darkest and most dangerous after sundown
Interview Con Edison on repair schedule and whether they've received bulk work orders
Cover resident concerns: How has darkness affected street safety, foot traffic, or business activity?

themes_detail.label: Homeless Crisis Requests Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints reached 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 471% spike from the 0.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.45), indicating possible encampment growth or service gaps in CD206.
evidence: 5 homeless person assistance complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% increase)
Z-score of 4.45 indicates statistically significant spike
Community Board has requested funding for senior center programs and additional school social services, suggesting pre-existing service gaps
No current-week follow-up data; unclear if trend persists or resolved
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Identify encampment locations and interview unhoused residents on what precipitated recent arrivals
Contact DHS and NYC Street Outreach on engagement numbers and resources deployed to CD206 in recent weeks
Community impact: Are residents reporting safety concerns, sanitation issues, or strain on local services?
